comparison_or_audit.report:
Aggregate of 5 evidence fragments; not acceptance.

Fresh fragment observations (source-only-security phase) covering all five input fragments. These are observations derived in this phase, not prior reviews or acceptance.

Fragment 1: Source implements secure descriptor-relative immutable generation: openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (fallback to componentwise O_NOFOLLOW), consistent O_NOFOLLOW opens, st_dev/st_ino verification post-open (TOCTOU defense), hard-link rejection (st_nlink!=1), mode normalization to 0444/0555 (no setuid/sticky), atomic RENAME_NOREPLACE, and parent-fsync durability handling. Tests cover publishing, mode preservation, directory bounds, root overlap, symlink rejection, zero bounds. Test for hard links/special entries/manifest mismatches is truncated in fragment, so full coverage of those cases is not visible. No concrete security vulnerabilities identified in provided source.

Fragment 2: Security observations: (1) enforcement::inspect_and_promote_cache copies files directly into project-cache, uses a hardcoded downloaded-crate byte check, and lacks RENAME_NOREPLACE/staging/immutable generation, conflicting with lib.rs claims and the cache tests shown. (2) Network guard proxy sets https_proxy/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY but only parses http:// absolute-form requests and never handles CONNECT, so HTTPS package sources will not be proxied correctly. (3) check_file_size_exceeded and check_scratch_size_exceeded only inspect top-level directory entries, missing files in subdirectories. (4) system_layout add_entry preserves symlinks without resolving targets; a symlink under /usr or /lib can point to a bound workspace/grant path, potentially bypassing the read-only system filter. (5) safe_prlimit ignores errors, so resource limits may be silently absent. Missing evidence: cache.rs, validation.rs, probe.rs, protocol.rs, and full origin.rs parser are not in this fragment.

Fragment 3: src/origin.rs `is_public_address` classifies IPv6 6to4/Teredo/NAT64 addresses as public, so encapsulated private/loopback addresses can pass production resolved authorization. src/probe.rs `probe()` sets `new_session` and `parent_death_signal` true without verifying them, only checking /proc/self/ns existence, overstating capabilities. `locate_backend()` accepts any PATH file named bwrap without ownership/permission checks, allowing an attacker-controlled PATH entry to be hashed and approved. src/validation.rs writable grant symlink check is immediate-only, not recursive, so nested symlinks can escape scope. Environment validation omits RUSTC_WRAPPER, CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI, and writable PATH entries, enabling arbitrary execution or network bypass.

Fragment 4: Source enforces canonical absolute paths (no traversal, NUL, trailing slash), HTTPS-only network origins, immutable git revisions, and phase-bound read-write access. Environment allowlist blocks proxy/credential injection. Identity derivation binds grants to endpoints, preventing substitution. Missing: grant overlap/uniqueness checks, origin parser details, and Bubblewrap enforcement are outside fragment. Dangling symlink lexical normalization may permit escape if target later changes; no cross-fragment context to confirm mitigation.

Fragment 5: Fragment 5 supplies only Rust tests and digests; no runner, validation, origin, or Bubblewrap source is present, so enforcement correctness is unverified. Tests show fail-closed legacy rejection, administrative PATH/grant exclusion, reserved /.galla-sandbox, loopback/alias/overlap rejection, golden identity vectors, schema/parser parity, host-permission and rustup-state immutability, and nested-sandbox guard. Missing evidence: valid_request/cargo fixture definitions, validation::parse_and_validate implementation, identity verification against source content, mount/read-only enforcement, cache promotion, lockfile handling, and runner source. Grant identity values appear arbitrary (e.g., digest(b\"extra\")) with no test proving they bind to source bytes. Ignored e2e tests (system toolchains, rustup) do not provide runnable security evidence. No discrepancy requiring arbitration in this fragment.

Decision flags: Fragments 2 and 3 require human arbitration due to concrete security discrepancies and missing evidence. Fragments 1, 4, and 5 do not. Overall decision_required=true.
